object_description: low-profile school volume with a collective atrium
design_condition: The volume is positioned close to the river on the west and kept lower toward the surrounding landscape, while the southern and eastern edges structure open spaces around the school and sports hall.

positive.statement: The external spatial structure integrates the three-story volume into its surroundings.
The inner large space as a collective center with surrounding spatial units is convincingly received.
The walkway, river promenade, school garden, and flexible space beside the sports hall create a coherent landscape structure.
The cascade-like atrium creates a large-scale spatial experience and intelligently illuminates the auditorium with sidelight.
The communicative experience in the hall and the horizontal networking of class units are remarkably preserved.
The internal school landscape offers exemplary academic and operational advantages.
The proposed timber skeletal construction with composite ceilings is a promising construction method.
The compact building and technical concept indicate good economic efficiency in construction and operation.

negative.statement: The two dominant spiral staircases are insufficient because of their narrow width and platform-less solution.
The music department is located in a secondary basement position with an unattractive corridor.
The expression is somewhat brittle and refers to pragmatic local buildings.
The acoustic requirements along the street remain unresolved.
Any expansion into a sports hall would be operationally unfavorable and is more of a temporary solution.
The fire protection requirements have not yet been fully clarified.
The revised school garden and greenhouse arrangement remains rather random in relation to the facade.
The movement flow toward the river is not clearly slowed by the side ends of the vestibule.
